"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 3328: a near-silent unit with two clear responses.

1. First token of a document (the model has no earlier context there): its value is
   token-dependent and mostly small and negative, more negative for longer tokens. A document
   opening with "Title" (a metadata-style record header) gives a strong positive value.
2. The keyword "switch" (or "match") opening a branch statement in code, i.e. right after
   indentation or a line break: a clear negative value. In prose the same word is near zero.
Everywhere else the program predicts 0 (that part of the activation is diffuse and not
captured by any simple rule).
"""

READS = ()

TITLE_START = 1.16        # first token "Title" of a document
START_PER_BYTE = -0.027   # first-token value per UTF-8 byte of the token
SWITCH_VALUE = -0.6       # "switch" / "match" opening a code statement
KEYWORDS = {"switch": -0.6, "match": -0.5}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    t = prefix.position
    new_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    value = 0.0
    if new_document:
        if word == "Title":
            value = TITLE_START
        else:
            value = START_PER_BYTE * len(token.encode("utf-8"))
    elif word in KEYWORDS and t > 0:
        before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
        if before.strip() == "" or before.endswith(("\n", "{", "\t")):
            value = KEYWORDS[word]
    return carry, float(value)

"""English ordinal endings, with weaker responses for symbolic ordinals.

Strongest on the ending of 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, etc.; not on the
numeral itself. Whitespace weakens the response. A small positive
startup offset depends on whitespace and control-token boundaries.
"""
import re

READS = ()
STRENGTH = {'st': 1.13, 'nd': 1.19, 'rd': 1.18, 'th': 0.93}
NUMBER = re.compile(r'(?<![\w])([0-9]+)(\s*(?:\^\{?|<sup>)?\s*)$')
VARIABLE = re.compile(r'\b[nkij]\s*$')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    tail = '' if first else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    ending = token.strip().lstrip('-')
    value = 0.0
    if first:
        value = 0.16
        if token.startswith('<|'):
            value = -0.25
        elif token.isascii() and token.strip().isalpha():
            value = 0.08 if token[:1].isspace() else 0.30
    if ending in STRENGTH:
        number = NUMBER.search(tail)
        if first:
            value = 1.0
        elif number:
            n = int(number[1][-2:])
            expected = ('th' if 11 <= n <= 13 else
                        {1: 'st', 2: 'nd', 3: 'rd'}.get(n % 10, 'th'))
            value = STRENGTH[ending] if ending == expected else 0.2
            if token[:1].isspace() or number[2].isspace():
                value *= 0.75
        elif ending == 'th' and VARIABLE.search(tail):
            value = 0.55 if token.startswith('-') else 0.3
    return (doc, (tail + token)[-64:]), value

"""Ordinal-suffix detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj component 3330.

What it does: the component fires on the suffix token of an ordinal number written
with digits: the "th" in "19th", "st" in "21st", "nd" in "2nd", "rd" in "3rd". It is
about 1 there and near 0 on almost every other token. It also has a weaker, roughly
constant bump on the first token of a document, where the activation averages a
little above zero (about 0.16). Everything else is predicted as 0.

Main logic, token by token:
  1. If the token (leading space ignored) is one of st, nd, rd, th, and the token
     before it ends in a digit, predict ORDINAL.
  2. If the token is the first of its document (first token of the row, or the
     document id has just changed), add DOC_START.
"""

READS = ()

ORDINAL_SUFFIXES = {"st", "nd", "rd", "th"}
ORDINAL = 1.0      # typical activation on "19|th", "21|st", "2|nd", "3|rd"
DOC_START = 0.16   # small average bump on a document's first token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    value = 0.0
    if len(prefix) > 1:
        previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
        if token in ORDINAL_SUFFIXES and previous[-1:].isdigit():
            value += ORDINAL
        if prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
            value += DOC_START
    else:
        value += DOC_START
    return carry, value

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 3331.

What it does, in plain terms: a weak, diffuse feature that is nearly silent over
most text. Its largest, most reliable responses are:

1. The first token of a text (the first token of a packed row, or the first token
   after a document break). With no context to read, its value depends on what the
   token is: positive for lowercase words, digits, symbols and spaces; near zero or
   negative for capitalised words and non-Latin scripts.
2. The word "time" in the sense "this time" / "that time" (strongest), and more
   weakly any other "time".
3. A few words that push it up ("last", "chance", "value", "range") and a few that
   push it down ("un" as in Italian "un", "public", "fun").
4. "of" right after an example/evidence noun ("photo of", "chance of", "evidence of").

Everything else is predicted as 0. Predictions are in the component's own units
(its activation, roughly -1 to +1.5).
"""
READS = ()

THIS_THAT = ("this", "that")
UP_WORDS = {"last": 0.3, "chance": 0.3, "value": 0.15, "range": 0.15}
DOWN_WORDS = {"un": -0.2, "public": -0.15, "fun": -0.15}
EXAMPLE_NOUNS = ("photo", "photos", "chance", "example", "examples", "evidence", "shot")


def first_token_value(s, row_start):
    """Value at the first token of a text, where the model has no context."""
    if not s.isascii():
        return -0.05
    body = s.strip()
    if not body or not body[0].isalnum() or body[0].isdigit() or s[:1] == " ":
        return 0.3 if row_start else 0.2
    return 0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix) == 1:  # first token of the row
        return None, first_token_value(tok, True)
    if prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:  # first token of a document
        return None, first_token_value(tok, False)
    word = tok.strip().lower()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    if word == "of" and prev in EXAMPLE_NOUNS:
        return None, 0.4
    if word == "time":
        return None, 1.0 if prev in THIS_THAT else 0.15
    if word in UP_WORDS:
        return None, UP_WORDS[word]
    return None, DOWN_WORDS.get(word, 0.0)

"""A detector for AM/PM endings and short fragments of the letter sequence am.

Clock markers get a large response, especially after minutes. Quieter
responses cover am fragments, the amin(e) root, and short continuations of
an unfinished am word. Transliteration also recognizes this sequence in
Greek, Cyrillic and kana. An opening Title: label has a separate negative
response. A short text tail is reset at document boundaries.
"""
import re
import regex
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
_CLOCK = re.compile(r'(\d{1,2})([:.]\d{2}){0,2}\s*[ap]\.?m\.?$', re.I)
_DOTTED = re.compile(r'(?:^|\W)[ap]\.m\.?$', re.I)
_SCRIPTS = regex.compile(
    r'[\p{Latin}\p{Greek}\p{Cyrillic}\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}]+'
)
# Rounded activation means for named patterns in training text.
VALUES = {
    'after_am_consonant': 0.56,
    'after_am_vowel': 0.82,
    'am_capital': 1.84,
    'am_fragment': 1.55,
    'am_non_ascii': 1.31,
    'am_plus_vowel': 1.28,
    'long_or_common_am': 0.09,
    'amine_root': 3.09,
    'background': 0.0,
    'clock_hour': 5.72,
    'clock_minutes': 10.12,
    'contains_am': 0.35,
    'dotted_hour': 8.5,
    'dotted_marker': 6.49,
    'dotted_minutes': 11.07,
    'dotted_uppercase_clock': 5.22,
    'ends_am': 0.32,
    'english_copula': -0.05,
    'iam_fragment': 1.34,
    'joins_a_m': 1.98,
    'opening_title_colon': -8.33,
    'pm_other': 0.45,
}


@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def fragment(token):
    s = token.strip()
    low = anyascii(s).lower()
    if low in ('am', 'pm'):
        if low == 'pm':
            return 'pm_other'
        if not s.isascii():
            return 'am_non_ascii'
        return 'am_capital' if s[:1].isupper() else 'am_fragment'
    if 'am' not in low:
        return 'background'
    if len(low) > 6 or zipf_frequency(low, 'en') >= 4.0:
        return 'long_or_common_am'
    if re.fullmatch(r'.?amin(?:e|es|s)?', low):
        return 'amine_root'
    if re.fullmatch(r'am[aeiou]', low):
        return 'am_plus_vowel'
    if low == 'iam':
        return 'iam_fragment'
    if low.endswith('am'):
        return 'ends_am'
    return 'contains_am'


def category(before, token):
    if before == 'Title' and token == ':':
        return 'opening_title_colon'
    s = token.strip()
    low = s.lower()
    text = before + token
    clock = _CLOCK.search(text)
    if 'm' in low and clock:
        if s.startswith('.') and 'M' in s:
            return 'dotted_uppercase_clock'
        if s.startswith('.'):
            return 'dotted_minutes' if clock.group(2) else 'dotted_hour'
        return 'clock_minutes' if clock.group(2) else 'clock_hour'
    if 'm' in low and _DOTTED.search(text):
        return 'dotted_marker'
    if token == ' am' and re.search(r'\bI$', before):
        return 'english_copula'
    # A short continuation can join the a and m across a token boundary.
    joined = before[-1:] + s
    if not token[:1].isspace() and 0 < len(s) <= 5:
        # Recognize the amin(e) root even when split after a or am.
        if before.lower().endswith(('a', 'am')):
            if re.search(r'amin(?:e|es|s)?$', text.lower()):
                return 'amine_root'
        if _SCRIPTS.fullmatch(joined):
            if anyascii(before[-1:]).lower().endswith('a'):
                if anyascii(s).lower().startswith('m'):
                    return 'joins_a_m'
        if s.isalpha() and before.lower().endswith('am'):
            return 'after_am_vowel' if low[0] in 'aeiou' else 'after_am_consonant'
    return fragment(token)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = VALUES.get(category(before, token), 0.0)
    return (doc, (before + token)[-60:]), value

"""A spelling-sensitive rail/trail feature, not a general motion detector.

Whole-token rail(s), trail(s), and track(s) go negative. Split r+ail,
ra+il, and tr+ack also go negative; str+us and construed/stru go positive.
Longer single tokens such as railway do not trigger the rail rule.
Other negative rules cover HTML tr, tr near Vietnamese-like diacritics,
traditional vehicle-character bytes, 軌/軌道, 追/追求, and Thai รำ.
The carry retains 32 bytes and the age of a distinctive diacritic,
resetting at document boundaries. Unmatched tokens get a small baseline.
"""
import re
import unicodedata

READS = ()

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, b'', 100)
    _, tail, age = carry
    b = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    s = b.decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    before = tail.decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    joined = (tail + b).decode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    new_text = joined[len(before):]
    for ch in new_text:
        name = unicodedata.name(ch, '')
        if ch in 'đĐ' or ('LATIN' in name and any(mark in name for mark in
                ('HORN', 'BREVE', 'HOOK ABOVE', 'DOT BELOW'))):
            age = 0
            break
    piece, previous = s.lower(), before.lower()
    word = piece.strip()
    value = 0.002
    if word in ('rail', 'rails'):
        value = -6.6
    elif word in ('trail', 'trails'):
        value = -3.6
    elif word in ('track', 'tracks'):
        value = -1.0
    elif word in ('construed', 'stru'):
        value = 2.9
    elif previous.endswith('r') and piece.startswith('ail'):
        value = -7.3 if s.isupper() else -2.7
    elif previous.endswith('ra') and piece.startswith('il'):
        value = -2.9
    elif previous.endswith('tr') and piece.startswith('ack'):
        value = -2.6
    elif previous.endswith('str') and piece == 'us':
        value = 4.0
    elif word == 'tr' and re.search(r'</?\s*$', before):
        value = -2.5
    elif age < 32 and word == 'tr':
        value = -3.2
    # UTF-8 prefix around the traditional vehicle radical 車.
    elif b == b'\xe8\xbb':
        value = -2.6
    elif new_text and joined.endswith('軌'):
        value = -7.3
    elif joined.endswith('軌道') and new_text == '道':
        value = -2.6
    elif s in ('追', '追求'):
        value = -3.0
    elif new_text and joined.endswith('รำ'):
        value = -6.3
    return (doc, (tail + b)[-32:], min(age + 1, 100)), value

"""Rail / track / trail detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3334.

In plain terms: this component is a "track" feature. Its activation goes strongly
negative on the token for a rail (" rail", " rails", "Rail"), and negative on the
pieces of "trail" and "track" words (" trail", "TRAIL", "trak", "ailing" in "tr|ailing",
" track", " tracks"). The same idea appears in other languages: Chinese 轨 (track),
追 / 追求 / 追逐 / 追寻 / 追踪 (chase, pursue, track down), Korean 추 (as in 추적, chase),
and Japanese ール (the end of レール, rail). The one clear positive case is " construed"
("shall be construed"). Every other token predicts 0.

The program looks only at the current token, so it needs no carried state and no context.
"""

READS = ()

# The word for a rail: the strongest negative activations.
RAIL_WORDS = {"rail": -6.0, "rails": -7.0, "Rail": -5.0, "Rails": -6.0, "railing": -2.5}

# Trail and the pieces of trail-like words: negative.
TRAIL_WORDS = {
    "trail": -4.0,
    "Trail": -4.0,
    "trails": -3.2,
    "trak": -3.0,
    "AIL": -3.0,
    "ailing": -1.9,
    "ailer": -1.5,
    "ails": -1.1,
    "trailing": -0.8,
    "trailer": -0.5,
}

# Track: weaker negative. "tr" is the first piece of many track and trail words.
TRACK_WORDS = {"track": -1.1, "Track": -1.3, "tracks": -1.3, "Tracks": -1.5, "tr": -0.4}

# The same concept in other languages: track, rail, chase, pursue.
OTHER_LANGUAGES = {
    "轨": -8.0,
    "追": -3.6,
    "追求": -2.4,
    "追逐": -1.0,
    "追寻": -0.9,
    "追踪": -0.7,
    "추": -2.3,
    "ール": -0.8,
}

# The one clear positive case: legal "shall be construed".
POSITIVE_WORDS = {"construed": 2.9}

VALUES = {
    **RAIL_WORDS,
    **TRAIL_WORDS,
    **TRACK_WORDS,
    **OTHER_LANGUAGES,
    **POSITIVE_WORDS,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predicted activation at the newest token: its table value, or 0 for any other token."""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    return carry, float(VALUES.get(token, 0.0))

programs.sol:
"""Approximate rare UTF-8-fragment responses and document-start offsets.

After a space, an unfinished character is classified by averaging over its
possible final bytes. Han radicals (especially tree and grass), scripts,
and a few Hangul consonant/vowel groups set the response. This is a partial
model: individual byte prefixes within each group can differ substantially.
Initial-token text shape, speaker/addressee forms, and comment/control
punctuation supply a separate offset, retained through initial repetitions.
Smaller rules cover completed fragments and runs of middle dots.
"""
import math
import unicodedata as ud
from functools import lru_cache
import unihan

READS = ()
RADICAL_RESPONSE = {
    'tree': 5.6,
    'grass': 2.7,
    'boat': 3.5,
    'lack': -4.0,
    'gold': 1.2,
    'water': 0.7,
    'clothes': 1.5,
    'speech': 0.7,
    'gate': 0.8,
    'sun': 0.8,
}


def single_character(data):
    try:
        s = data.decode('utf-8')
        return s if len(s) == 1 else ''
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return ''


def character_response(ch):
    name = ud.name(ch, '')
    if name.startswith('CJK UNIFIED IDEOGRAPH'):
        radical = unihan.radical_name(unihan.radical(ch))
        return RADICAL_RESPONSE.get(radical, 0.1)
    if ud.category(ch) == 'So' and ord(ch) >= 0x1F000:
        return 0.8
    if name.startswith(('GREEK', 'RUNIC', 'ETHIOPIC')):
        return 1.0
    if name.startswith('HANGUL SYLLABLE'):
        # Standard Unicode Hangul decomposition into onset and vowel.
        n = ord(ch) - 0xAC00
        onset, vowel = n // 588, n % 588 // 28
        if onset == 5:  # rieul
            return 1.8
        if onset == 1 and vowel in (18, 19):  # kk + eu/yi
            return -5.0
        if onset == 4 and vowel in (3, 4, 17, 18):  # selected tt combinations
            return -3.0
        return 0.0
    return 0.1


@lru_cache(maxsize=1024)
def fragment_response(partial):
    ch = single_character(partial)
    if ch:
        return character_response(ch)
    possibilities = [single_character(partial + bytes([b]))
                     for b in range(128, 192)]
    values = [character_response(c) for c in possibilities if c]
    return sum(values) / len(values) if values else 0.0


def initial_response(s):
    u = s.strip()
    if s == '\r':
        return 4.4
    if u == '//':  # an empty line comment versus its opening delimiter alone
        return 3.6 if '\n' in s else -0.85
    if u.lower() in {'i', 'my'}:
        return 1.0
    if u.lower() in {'you', 'your'}:
        return 1.2
    return (0.05 + 0.20 * s.isascii() - 0.09 * s.startswith(' ')
            + 0.16 * u.isupper() + 0.09 * u.islower()
            + 0.12 * u.istitle() + 0.17 * u.isdigit()
            + 0.07 * (bool(u) and not any(c.isalnum() for c in u))
            + 0.27 * ('\n' in s or '\r' in s)
            + 0.04 * math.log1p(len(u)))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    b, doc = prefix.token_bytes[-1], prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = prefix.position == 0 or doc != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    s = b.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    if s and not s.strip('·'):
        return None, 1.2
    if first:
        value = initial_response(s)
        return (doc, b, value), value
    if carry is not None and carry[:2] == (doc, b):
        return carry, carry[2]
    if len(b) != 1 or not 128 <= b[0] < 192:
        return None, 0.0
    previous = prefix.token_bytes[-2]
    spaced_lead = (len(previous) == 2 and previous[0] == 32
                   and 224 <= previous[1] < 240)
    spaced_emoji = previous.startswith(b' \xf0') and len(previous) in (3, 4)
    if spaced_lead or spaced_emoji:
        return None, fragment_response(previous[1:] + b)
    # A smaller echo on the final continuation byte of the same character.
    if prefix.position >= 2 and prefix.document_ids[-3] == doc:
        lead = prefix.token_bytes[-3]
        if (len(previous) == 1 and len(lead) == 2 and lead[0] == 32
                and 224 <= lead[1] < 240):
            partial = lead[1:] + previous
            ch = single_character(partial + b)
            if ch:
                scale = 0.5 if ud.name(ch, '').startswith('HANGUL') else 0.1
                return None, scale * fragment_response(partial)
    # Completed, split wood-radical characters without a separate space prefix.
    ch = single_character(previous + b)
    if len(previous) == 2 and ch and unihan.radical(ch) == 75:
        return None, 0.4
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 3336: a weak, lexical detector for the letter pair "ea".

Plain-terms description:
- It goes negative on text pieces spelled with "ea": tea, beach, meat, head, read, reach,
  clear, dream, ready, East. It is more negative when the piece continues a word begun in
  an earlier token (e.g. "Re" + "ach"), because a word fragment is where it fires hardest.
- It goes more negative on short letter-only fragments that continue a word, such as
  "a", "am", "art", "ach", "ae", "ats", "ason" (pieces of split words and names).
- It goes to +0.84 on the run of middle dots "··" used as dot leaders.
- Everything else predicts about 0.

The weights are least-squares fits to the component's activation on training rows.
What it misses: most of the variance is a few very large negative spikes on "a"-type
fragments inside unusual, split names or code tokens, and whether a fragment is a real
word or not. Nothing here captures that, so the program explains only a small share.
Tested on held-out training rows it explains about 5% of activation variance
(eval: 4.5%, Pearson r 0.21). A per-token lookup table would explain about 10%,
but it is a table of token ids with no concept behind it.
The program keeps no state beyond the previous token.
"""

READS = ()

DOT_LEADER = "··"
FRAGMENTS = {"a", "am", "an", "at", "as", "ae", "ar", "al", "ac", "ag", "ad", "af", "art", "ach", "aly", "are", "ats", "ason", "ea"}


def _continues_word(prefix):
    """True if this token has no leading space and follows a letter-ending token."""
    if len(prefix) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return False
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    return word[:1].isalpha() and not word.startswith(" ") and previous[-1:].isalpha()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if word == DOT_LEADER:
        return None, 0.84
    value = 0.0
    continues = _continues_word(prefix)
    if "ea" in word.lower():
        value += -0.34 if continues else -0.16
    if continues and word.strip().lower() in FRAGMENTS:
        value += -0.16
    return None, value

"""Column-padding detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3337.

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on the run of spaces or
tabs that pads text out to a column *in the middle of a line*, the kind of
alignment padding found in tables, `ls`-style listings, SQL column
definitions and aligned struct/dict literals (e.g. `Type:      value`,
`id      int     not null`). Ordinary indentation at the start of a line,
single spaces and prose give about zero.

The program follows each line as it is written. For every whitespace-only
token of two or more characters that comes after some text on the same
line, it predicts a negative value, larger when:
  * the run is wide (4 or more characters), and
  * the line above also had two or more such padding runs (so this line is
    part of an aligned table or column block), or this is the second
    padding run in the line (a row of columns).
Everything else is predicted as 0.
"""

READS = ()


def _is_padding(tok):
    # a run of two or more spaces/tabs with no line break
    return len(tok) >= 2 and tok.strip() == "" and "\n" not in tok


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    st = carry
    if st is None or st["doc"] != doc:
        # new document: forget the lines before it
        st = {"doc": doc, "has_text": False, "pads": 0, "prev_pads": 0}

    value = 0.0
    if _is_padding(tok) and st["has_text"]:
        wide = len(tok) >= 4
        aligned = st["prev_pads"] >= 2
        second = st["pads"] == 1
        if wide and aligned:
            value = -4.0
        elif aligned:
            value = -1.3
        elif wide and second:
            value = -2.9
        elif wide:
            value = -0.6
        else:
            value = -0.15

    # update the line state with this token
    st = dict(st)
    if _is_padding(tok) and st["has_text"]:
        st["pads"] += 1
    if "\n" in tok:
        parts = tok.split("\n")
        st["prev_pads"] = st["pads"] if len(parts) == 2 else 0
        st["pads"] = 0
        st["has_text"] = parts[-1].strip() != ""
    elif tok.strip() != "":
        st["has_text"] = True
    return st, float(value)

"""Local cues for enumeration, kinds, and restricted choices.

Abstract list nouns get positive gains after counts, question words, or
'following'; two-way alternatives get an extra gain. Singular descriptions
and purpose phrases provide a smaller negative contrast. This is a partial
approximation, using three preceding tokens and resetting at each document.
"""
from functools import lru_cache

READS = ()
# Noun classes: words, singular baseline, plural baseline, counted boost.
NOUNS = (
    ('type kind category sort', -.02, .22, .66),
    ('way method approach option choice possibility scenario case situation',
     .01, .27, 1.23),
    ('thing reason circumstance', .17, .66, 1.04),
    ('information group solution factor condition action item step example '
     'point aspect area location place purpose outcome consequence instance '
     'source setting pathway value structure feature issue question benefit '
     'problem characteristic result difference element component form part',
     -.01, .06, .20),
)
NOUNS = tuple((set(words.split()), a, b, c) for words, a, b, c in NOUNS)
COUNTS = set('two three four five six seven eight nine ten'.split())
QUANTIFIERS = set(('several various many few multiple different other '
                   'distinct more').split())


def singular(w):
    if w.endswith('ies'):
        return w[:-3] + 'y'
    return w[:-1] if w.endswith('s') else w


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def activation(w, p, q, r):
    root = singular(w)
    counted = p in COUNTS or (p.isdecimal() and 1 < int(p) <= 20)
    v = -.003
    for words, one, many, boost in NOUNS:
        if root not in words:
            continue
        v += many if root != w else one
        if counted: v += boost + (1.17 if p == 'two' else 0)
        elif q in COUNTS: v += .86
        if p in QUANTIFIERS: v += .43
        if p in {'what', 'which'}: v += .87
        if p == 'following': v += 1.28
        if p == 'only': v += 1.16
        if p == 'of' and q in {'number', 'variety', 'range'}: v += .61
        break
    if w == 'following' and p == 'the':
        v += .47 + (1.64 if q == 'of' else 0)
    if w == 'of':
        if singular(p) in NOUNS[0][0]:
            v += 1.30 if singular(p) != p else .27
            if q in COUNTS or r in COUNTS: v += 1.40
            if q in {'what', 'which'}: v += 2.48
            if q in {'a', 'some'}: v -= .85
        if p in {'summary', 'measure', 'share', 'amount'}: v -= .24
    if w in {'main', 'broad'} and counted: v += 1.83
    if w in {'possible', 'distinct', 'major', 'additional'} and counted:
        v += .85
    if w in COUNTS and (p == 'only' or (p == 'of' and q == 'one')):
        v += 1.55
    if w == 'choice' and p in {'no', 'only'}: v += 3.06
    if w == 'to' and p in {'what', 'which'}: v += 1.01
    if w == 'else' and p == 'what': v += 3.53
    if w in {'short', 'possible'} and p in {'a', 'an', 'very'}: v -= .93
    if w == 'sort' and p in {'a', 'some'}: v -= 1.20
    if w == 'to' and p in {'something', 'nothing', 'chance', 'opportunity',
                           'priority', 'link', 'easy', 'simple', 'key'}:
        v -= .50
    if w == 'for' and p in {'stands', 'stand', 'stood', 'term', 'acronym',
                            'abbreviation', 'synonym', 'expression', 'reputation'}:
        v -= 1.03
    if w in {'以下', '如下', '下列', '如何',
             '怎么', '怎麼', '怎', 'как'}:
        v += .47
    return v


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    history = carry[1] if carry and carry[0] == doc else ('', '', '')
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    return (doc, (word, *history[:2])), activation(word, *history)

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3339: the "be able to" detector.

It reads the word just written. It fires on an adjective that completes a
"be / been / being / was / were + ADJECTIVE" frame, and above all on "able"
("will be able to", "was able to", "been able to"). Weaker, but the same
idea, for "possible", "interested", "willing", "unable", "sure", "surprised"
and "impossible" (all words that are normally followed by "to" or a
"to"-infinitive). The same word after "is / are", "as", or an adverb gives
much less. "want" after a modal ("may want to", "might want to") also fires.
Everywhere else it predicts 0.

The numbers are its average activation on those words in training text.
"""

READS = ()

BE_FORMS = {" be", " being", " been", " was", " were", " become", " became"}

# Typical activation on the adjective when it follows a be-form.
ADJ_AFTER_BE = {
    " able": 7.3,
    " possible": 4.6,
    " interested": 3.7,
    " willing": 3.1,
    " unable": 2.9,
    " sure": 2.1,
    " surprised": 1.8,
    " impossible": 1.1,
}

# "want" right after a modal: "may want to", "might want to".
MODALS = {" may", " might", "'d", " will", " well", " also"}
MODAL_WANT = 3.0

# Share of that value when the word follows something other than a be-form.
OFF_FRAME = 0.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    if word == " want" and prev in MODALS:
        return carry, MODAL_WANT
    if word not in ADJ_AFTER_BE:
        return carry, 0.0
    value = ADJ_AFTER_BE[word]
    if prev not in BE_FORMS:
        value *= OFF_FRAME
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 3340: a weak, mostly lexical feature.

Plain-language summary of what it responds to (checked on training rows):
  * the first token of each document (the token right after <|endoftext|>), where the
    activation is a fixed function of the token alone; mildly positive on average;
  * a UTF-8 byte fragment: one piece of a character the tokenizer split into bytes
    (it decodes alone to U+FFFD). These are most positive when the surrounding text is
    Greek, and are unremarkable in Japanese, Korean or Cyrillic text;
  * Thai script tokens, which are positive on average but very inconsistent.
Everything else is near zero.

The program follows the script of the last complete non-ASCII character in the document
(within the last 40 tokens) and predicts a small value from these three rules.
"""
import unicodedata

READS = ()

WINDOW = 40          # tokens over which a script still counts as the current context
DOC_START = 0.11     # first token of a document
FRAG_GREEK = 0.13    # byte fragment inside Greek text
FRAG_OTHER = 0.02    # byte fragment in other or unknown context
THAI = 0.04          # Thai script token


def _script(ch):
    name = unicodedata.name(ch, "")
    return name.split()[0] if name else "UNKNOWN"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    doc = prefix.document_ids
    new_doc = t == 0 or doc[t] != doc[t - 1]
    if new_doc or carry is None:
        script, age = None, WINDOW + 1
    else:
        script, age = carry
        age += 1
    text = prefix.token_strings[t]
    value = 0.0
    if new_doc:
        value = DOC_START
    if "�" in text:
        # a byte fragment: not a complete character on its own
        if script == "GREEK" and age <= WINDOW:
            value = FRAG_GREEK
        else:
            value = FRAG_OTHER
    elif any("฀" <= ch <= "๿" for ch in text):
        value = THAI
    # a complete non-ASCII character here becomes the new script context
    for ch in text:
        if ord(ch) > 127 and ch != "�":
            script, age = _script(ch), 0
            break
    return (script, age), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3341 -- a "knowing" and "word-fragment" detector.

Mostly silent (near 0). It fires, with a sign, on three kinds of word pieces:

1. Hungarian abstract-noun suffix pieces "-ság / -ség" (English "-ness / -ity") split
   after an "s": "sebess|ég" (speed), "hatós|ág" (authority), "váls|ág" (crisis).
   Strongly positive (about +4.5); a lone "é" in the same spot is weaker (+2).
2. The verb "to know" in other languages, as word pieces: Chinese 知 / 知道 / 不知(道)
   and 明白 / 懂得, Vietnamese "biết", Romance "sab-/sap-/sais/sabe/saber", Dutch "weet".
   Negative, strongest on 不知 and 不知道 (about -6 to -7), about -2 to -4 otherwise.
3. Capital-letter acronym fragments after an all-caps token ending in S, as in
   "MS|B", "LS|B", "IS|AP": strongly negative (about -5).
   Also "SB"/"sb" pieces (-3 to -4) and a few other letter fragments (small).

Everything else predicts 0. The values are the typical activation for each piece,
not fitted to context, so a lookup of these pieces is the whole program.
"""

READS = ()

# "to know" (Chinese, Vietnamese, Romance, Dutch word pieces) and their typical activation.
KNOW = {
    "知": -2.0, "知道": -3.0, "不知": -7.0, "不知道": -6.0, "都知道": -3.0, "才知道": -5.0,
    "就知道": -3.0, "知道了": -3.0, "忘了": -2.5, "明白": -2.0, "懂得": -1.5, "未知": -1.0,
    " biết": -4.0, "biết": -4.0, " sab": -2.5, " sap": -2.5, " sais": -1.5, " sabe": -2.0,
    " saber": -1.0, "weet": -2.0,
}
# Letter fragments that are negative in general (acronym or foreign-word pieces).
FRAGMENT = {"SB": -4.0, " SB": -2.0, "sb": -3.5, " sb": -1.0, "AP": -0.6, "ap": -0.3,
            "bee": -1.5, "abo": -1.7}
# Hungarian -ság / -ság suffix pieces, when they follow a token ending in "s".
HUNGARIAN_SUFFIX = {"ág": 4.5, "ég": 4.5, "ét": 4.5, "át": 4.5, "é": 2.0}
# Acronym pieces after an all-caps token ending in S (e.g. "MS" + "B").
ACRONYM_SPLIT = {"B": -5.0, "AB": -5.0, "AP": -5.0, "BE": -5.0, "BA": -3.0, "BC": -3.0, "BI": -3.0}


def is_caps_ending_s(text):
    """An all-capital word of two or more letters that ends in S, such as 'MS' or 'IS'."""
    text = text.strip()
    return len(text) >= 2 and text.isalpha() and text.isupper() and text.endswith("S")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if cur in HUNGARIAN_SUFFIX and prev.endswith("s"):
        return carry, HUNGARIAN_SUFFIX[cur]
    if cur in ACRONYM_SPLIT and is_caps_ending_s(prev):
        return carry, ACRONYM_SPLIT[cur]
    if cur in KNOW:
        return carry, KNOW[cur]
    return carry, FRAGMENT.get(cur, 0.0)

"""A partial lexical approximation to a sensory/media-production feature.

Negative evidence comes from imaging, sound, physical appearance, coordinate
notation, and their units. Split word pieces are joined. A decaying media cue
supplies local context, with extra rules for frame rate and vector dimensions.
The fixed Title: and // header responses are document-start exceptions.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()
# Word families: name, contribution, and an English stem pattern.
FAMILIES = (
    ('imaging', -0.389, r'imag|photo|optic|cinema|footage'),
    ('video', -0.310, r'video|camera|visual|vision'),
    ('graphics', -0.414, r'graphic|render|texture|shader|canvas|glyph|font|logo|sprite'),
    ('illustration', -0.210, r'illustr|draw|paint|cartoon'),
    ('display', -0.046, r'screen|display|pictur|film'),
    ('audio', -0.399, r'audio|acoust|stereo|synth|waveform'),
    ('sound', -0.417, r'sound|noise|voice|vocal|tone'),
    ('music', -0.128, r'music|melod|harmon'),
    ('color', -0.304, r'colou?r|grayscale|rgb'),
    ('light', -0.267, r'light|bright|lumin'),
    ('image_quality', -0.603, r'resolut|blur|shad|aperture|sharp'),
    ('detail', -0.311, r'detail|contrast|enhanc|saturat'),
    ('beauty', -0.176, r'beaut|aesthet|realisti'),
    ('geometry', -0.141, r'spati|dimens|vector|perspect|project|ellipse|sphere|cubic'),
    ('transform', -0.384, r'transform|rotat|zoom|scale|mesh'),
    ('signal_processing', -0.260,
     r'amplit|frequen(?:cy|cies)|modulat|convolut|fourier|interpol|encoder|sensing|sensor'),
    ('body_surface', -0.293, r'eye|hair|finger|thumb|tooth|teeth|jaw|limb|shoulder'),
)
PATTERNS = tuple((name, weight, re.compile(r'^(?:'+pat+')', re.I))
                 for name, weight, pat in FAMILIES)

@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def lexical(raw):
    w = raw.strip()
    t = w.strip('._(<,/#:').lower()
    flags = {name: bool(p.match(t)) for name, _, p in PATTERNS}
    score = sum(weight for name, weight, _ in PATTERNS if flags[name])
    if wordnet.is_a(t, 'musical instrument'):
        score -= 0.020  # instrument
    if wordnet.is_a(t, 'color'):
        score -= 0.035  # color_name
    if '°' in w:
        score -= 0.559  # degree_symbol
    if t == 'px':
        score -= 0.700  # pixel_unit
    if t in ('deg', 'degree', 'degrees', 'radian', 'radians'):
        score -= 0.403  # angle_unit
    if t in ('hz', 'khz', 'mhz'):
        score -= 0.451  # frequency_unit
    if w == 'dB':
        score -= 0.873  # decibel
    if t in ('frame', 'frames'):
        score -= 0.524  # frame
    if t in ('edit', 'editing', 'edited'):
        score -= 0.346  # edit
    if t == 'ease':
        score -= 1.284  # ease
    if t in ('ratio', 'proportion', 'proportions'):
        score -= 0.296  # ratio
    if t in ('float', 'double'):
        score -= 0.257  # float
    if w in ('.x', '.y', '.z'):
        score -= 0.478  # coordinate
    if w.lower() in ('.png', '.jpg', '.jpeg', '.gif', '.bmp', '.svg'):
        score -= 0.337  # image_extension
    if t in ('gl', 'opengl', 'glfw', 'glm', 'pygame'):
        score -= 0.550  # graphics_api
    if w == '-quality':
        score -= 0.665  # hyphen_quality
    media = any(flags[n] for n in ('imaging', 'video', 'graphics',
                                  'illustration', 'display'))
    sound = any(flags[n] for n in ('audio', 'sound', 'music'))
    space = any(flags[n] for n in ('geometry', 'transform', 'signal_processing'))
    quality = any(flags[n] for n in ('color', 'light', 'image_quality', 'detail'))
    cue = any(flags[n] for n in ('imaging', 'video', 'graphics', 'illustration',
                                'audio', 'sound', 'color', 'light',
                                'image_quality', 'detail'))
    return score, media, sound, space, quality, cue


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, '', '', 0., '')
    _, pos, tail, prev, recent, old = carry
    value, media, sound, space, quality, cue = lexical(text)
    value -= 0.0048 + 0.419 * recent
    joined = tail + text if text[:1].isascii() and text[:1].isalpha() else text
    words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+', joined)
    word = words[-1].lower() if words else ''
    if tail and joined != text:
        _, jm, js, jg, _, _ = lexical(word)
        value -= 0.202*jm + 0.392*js
        value -= 0.230*jg
    value += recent * (1.206*media - 0.102*quality)
    value += recent * 0.168 * sound
    if word == 'rate' and prev in ('frame', 'frames'):
        value -= 2.871
    if word in ('edit', 'editing') and prev in ('video', 'film', 'audio'):
        value -= 2.264
    if text.strip() in ('2', '3', '4') and prev in ('vec', 'vector', 'cv'):
        value -= 1.233
    if text.strip() == 'D' and old.strip() in ('2', '3', '4'):
        value -= 1.087
    if word.endswith('bezier'):
        value -= 2.401
    if word == 'ease' and recent > .08:
        value += 0.202
    if pos == 0 and text.strip() == 'Title':
        value = .778
    if pos == 1 and text.strip() == ':' and prev == 'title':
        value = -7.229
    if pos == 0 and text == '//\n':
        value = 3.442
    # A token closes a word at spaces or punctuation.
    tail = word if text[-1:].isascii() and text[-1:].isalpha() else ''
    recent = .90*recent + .10*cue
    return (doc, pos+1, tail, word or prev, recent, text), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3342, a weak, diffuse component.

What it does, in plain terms:
- It goes negative on words from digital imaging, graphics, video and audio production
  ("rendering", "texture", "canvas", "video", "image", "lighting", "resolution", "zoom",
  "stereo", "mixer", ...) and on display and signal units ("px", "°", "degrees", "Hz", "dB",
  "RGB", "LED"). "3D" / "2D" (a "D" after a digit) is the strongest such case.
- It goes mildly positive on a few sports, entertainment and geometry nouns ("series", "team",
  "player", "season", "band", "album", "perpendicular", "points", "triangle").
- A document-initial "Title:" colon (the ":" right after "<|endoftext|>Title") is hugely
  negative, the single largest activation in the data.
- Everything else is near zero, and most of the variance is spread over thousands of
  ordinary tokens that no short word list captures.

The program predicts those few cases with fixed values. Its variance explained is small
(about 0.02 on eval); it is a readable account of the component's main directions, not a
full model of it.
"""
READS = ()

# Words from digital imaging, graphics, video and audio production (activation negative).
IMAGING = set("""graphics graphic graphical render rendering rendered renders renderer texture textures
shader shaders image images img imaging video videos animation animations animated animate
editing editor filter filters effect effects layer layers canvas stroke strokes brush brushes
font fonts color colors colour colours lighting light lights shadow shadows shade grayscale
contrast brightness saturation enhancement enhance resolution optical lens lenses camera cameras
photo photos photograph photography portrait footage frame frames zoom zoomed realistic mesh
sprite illustration illustrated painting paint drawing sculpt render blur blurred noise grain
aperture exposure perspective projection stereo stereophonic speaker speakers audio sound sounds
voice vocal vocals drums drum guitar guitarist piano synth wav waveform mixer mix mixing headphones
microphone bass amplifier acoustic multimedia fx transparent gradient gradients pixel pixels""".split())

# Display, angle and signal units (activation negative).
UNITS = {"°", "px", "deg", "degrees", "degree", "hz", "khz", "mhz", "db", "rgb", "led", "lcd", "ratio"}

# Sports, entertainment and geometry nouns (activation mildly positive).
POSITIVE = set("""series team player players season band album episode stadium studio studios drama
theatre theater league leagues perpendicular points point triangle centroid tangent theorem
coordinates""".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    tok = raw.strip().lower()
    # The colon right after a document-initial "Title": a very large negative activation.
    if len(prefix) >= 3 and raw == ":" and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "Title" \
            and prefix.token_strings[-3] == "<|endoftext|>":
        return carry, -7.0

    if tok == "d" and len(prefix) >= 2 and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().isdigit():
        return carry, -1.0
    if tok in UNITS or tok in IMAGING:

"""Digit "1" written as the units digit of a two-digit number.

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3343 fires on the digit token "1" when it comes right
after another digit, i.e. as the second digit of a number such as 11, 21, 31, 2019, 2104.
It is strongest when the first digit is 1 or 2 (about 3 nats-of-activation), weaker for
first digits 3 to 9 (about 1), slightly negative after a leading 0, and near zero when the
"1" is the first digit of a number. It is weaker still on a "1" deeper inside a long
digit string. Other tokens are predicted as 0.

The program keeps one number in its carry: how many digits in a row end just before the
current token, in the same document (a document change resets it).
"""

READS = ()

DIGITS = set("0123456789")

The preceding verb modulates the response: 'end up' is weak, while
'build up' and 'break up' are strong. Inflected verbs share their base form.
A smaller echo follows on determiners and prepositions.
Short u+p spellings across tokens and the Japanese loanword are included.
There is also a separate response to a document's initial 'Title:' heading.
Unmatched positions return zero; state resets at document boundaries.

from functools import lru_cache

import wordnet

# Groups of familiar up-constructions, from weak to strong.
VERB_GROUPS = (
    (0.9, 'end show be'),
    (1.4, 'speed'),
    (1.9, 'set pick wake grow get go'),
    (2.5, 'come give catch move wind check'),
    (3.1, 'make open follow heat mess'),
    (3.9, 'take bring keep hold stand sign walk step fire let'),
    (3.9, 'start line mark pop lay'),
    (4.4, 'mix'),
    (4.6, 'add sum look save back'),
    (5.5, 'clean put cover round pair lock light lead call'),
    (7.0, 'build break tear match pull fill roll'),
    (7.0, 'link team blow cut split hook'),
    (7.0, 'close dress blend'),
)

def verb_strength(word):
    word = word.lower()
    if word in VERBS:
        return VERBS[word]
    for base in wordnet.base_forms(word):
        if base in VERBS:
            return VERBS[base]
    if 'verb' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(word):
        return 4.0
    return None

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', 0, 0.0)

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    s = token.strip(' \t\r\n-_/.[()]')
    lower = s.lower()
    previous = re.search(r'([A-Za-z]+)$', tail)
    word = previous.group(1) if previous else ''
    value = 0.0
    up_now = False

    if lower in ('up', 'ups'):
        up_now = True
        strength = verb_strength(word)
        if word.lower() in ('it', 'him', 'her', 'us', 'them', 'me', 'you'):
            strength = 4.3
        elif word.lower() in ('the', 'a', 'an', 'of', 'to', 'for', 'and', 'or',
                               'at', 'in', 'by', 'as', 'with', 'can', 'could',
                               'will', 'would', 'should', 'may', 'might', 'must'):

                    or s.istitle())

            strength = 3.1 if boundary else 0.3

        if tail.endswith('\\'):
            value = -0.1
        if s.isupper():
            value *= 0.8
        elif s == 'Up' and token[:1].isalpha():
            value = 0.7 * value - 0.75
    elif lower.endswith(('up', 'ups')):
        root = lower[:-3] if lower.endswith('ups') else lower[:-2]
        strength = VERBS.get(root)
        if strength is not None:
            # Compounds such as 'backup', 'lookup', and 'setup'.
            value = -strength
            if root == 'hook':
                value = -4.1
            elif root in ('line', 'pick'):
                value = -3.5
            elif root == 'build':
                value = -4.5
            elif root == 'match':
                value = -3.0
            up_now = True

    elif lower == 'уп':
        value = -1.0
    elif token in ('п', 'П') and tail.lower().endswith('у'):
        value = -4.3
    elif (token.isalpha() and len(token) <= 2
          and token.lower().startswith('p') and tail.lower().endswith('u')):

    elif token == 'アップ':  # Japanese loanword "up".

        value = -10.4

        if token == ' the':
            value += 0.3 * last_up - 1.2
        elif token == ' a':
            value += 0.3 * last_up - 0.75
        elif token == ' of':
            value += min(0.0, 0.75 * last_up + 1.1)
        elif token in (' their', ' his', ' her'):

        elif token in (' my', ' your', ' our', ' its', ' an'):
            value += 0.2 * last_up - 0.2
        elif token == ' with':
            value -= 0.45
        elif token in (' on', ' into', ' in'):
            value += 0.08 * last_up
        elif token == ' to':
            value -= 0.07

    state = (doc, (tail + token)[-64:], position + 1,
             value if up_now else 0.0)
    return state, value

"""Layer 1 MLP unit 3345: a definite-article detector.

The unit writes a strong "this is a definite article" signal into the residual
stream. It is active on the article token itself, and nearly silent on everything
else (commas, nouns, verbs, other function words).

  * English " the" is the strongest case (about 1.4); " The" is about 1.05 and a
    bare "The" about 0.7. " THE" is about 1.0.
  * German articles fire too: " die" and " Die" (about 1.1), " der" (0.9),
    " den" and " das" (0.7), " dem" (0.5), capitalised " Der" / " Das" (0.75).
  * Romance articles fire weakly: " el" and " la" (about 0.3), " las", " le" (about 0.15).

Context changes the size on English/German articles. After a preposition
("in the", "from the", "about the", "into the") it is about 20% stronger. After a
copula or a quantifier ("is the", "was the", "all the", "or the") it is about
40% weaker. At the first token of a document it is off.

Everything else is predicted as 0.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical activation of each article token, from the training data.
ARTICLE_LEVEL = {
    # English
    " the": 1.4, " THE": 1.0, " The": 1.05, "The": 0.7,
    # German
    " die": 1.05, " Die": 1.1, "Die": 1.3, " der": 0.9, " Der": 0.75, "Der": 0.75,
    " den": 0.7, " das": 0.7, " Das": 0.75, " dem": 0.5,
    # Romance (weak)
    " el": 0.33, " la": 0.3, " las": 0.17, " le": 0.16, " los": 0.11,
}

# Words before the article that change how strongly it fires.
PREPOSITIONS = {" in", " on", " from", " into", " about", " between", " during",
                " by", " to", " for", " with", " at", " after", " through", " of"}
COPULAS = {" is", " are", " was", " were", " be", " been", " all", " this", " or", " what"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    level = ARTICLE_LEVEL.get(token, 0.0)
    if level == 0.0 or len(prefix) < 2:
        return carry, 0.0
    if prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0  # first token of a document
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    if before in PREPOSITIONS:
        level *= 1.2
    elif before in COPULAS:
        level *= 0.6
    return carry, level

                  and word.endswith(('en', 't')))

        value -= 0.09 + 0.72 * predicate
    if token in ('という', 'といった'):
        value -= 0.26
    if token == 'である':
        value -= 0.23
    return carry, float(value)

German function words appear in the last 30 tokens of the same document.

    "oder", "aber", "sondern", "sowie", "zu", "nicht", "niet", "ich", "sich", "sie", "es",

    "dat", "zijn", "ook", "kunnen", "moet", "hebben", "mir", "mich", "dich", "worden",
}

    "werden": -3.5, "lassen": -4.5, "sollte": -4.0, "sollen": -4.5, "soll": -5.0,
    "können": -3.0, "könnte": -5.0, "müssen": -4.0, "darf": -3.5, "wollen": -5.0,
    "will": -2.0, "wollte": -2.0, "kann": -2.3, "sollten": -3.5, "könnten": -4.0,

frequency dictionary suppresses English lookalikes. This is a spelling
heuristic, not a full morphological analysis. Initial formatting and
English articles have separate small rules. Everything else predicts zero.
"""

from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def romance_word(word):
    frequency = max(zipf_frequency(word, language)
                    for language in ('es', 'pt', 'it', 'fr', 'ro'))
    return frequency >= 3.0 and frequency > zipf_frequency(word, 'en') + 0.7

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != document
    stem = '' if first else carry[1]
    joined = bool(stem and token[:1].isalpha())
    match = re.search(r'[^\W\d_]+$', stem + token.lower())
    word = match[0][-80:] if match else ''
    carry = (document, word)

    if first:
        if token == '\n': return carry, 1.404
        if token.isspace(): return carry, 0.104
        if token.strip().lower() in ('a', 'an', 'the'): return carry, 0.646
        if token and not token.strip('#'): return carry, 0.607
        if token.strip() == '{': return carry, 0.906
        if token.isdecimal(): return carry, 0.109
        return carry, 0.0

    ending = token.lower()
    value = 0.0

        if re.fullmatch(r'(?:ante|ente|iente|anti|enti|ienti)s?', ending):

                return carry, 0.723 if romance_word(word) else 0.354

        elif ending in ('erte', 'orte', 'arte', 'orti', 'arti'):
            value = 0.96

                                  (stem.endswith('m') and stem[-2] in 'aou')):

                elif stem.endswith('ent'): value = 1.39

  "age" in "Voyage" gets nothing).

tokens that complete these spellings, and the same token gives little activation when
the pattern is absent. The table is the list of spellings with the mean activation
measured for each on training rows (a description of the data, not a verified mechanism).

and switching the program in for the component keeps ~82% of the zero-ablation KL.

    A pattern counts only if it ends inside the current token, so it fires once.

across fragments is stronger within words or across a hyphen, and
a preceding final 'ss' strengthens it further. 'sh' weakens the initial-s

counts digit 8s in the previous four tokens. This is a spelling-level
approximation, not a table of individual word-pair strengths.

    fragments = re.findall(r'[a-z]+', text)

    current = fragments[0] if fragments else ''

                  and text[0].isalpha())
    hyphenated = bool(tail and tail[-1].isalpha() and text.startswith('-'))

    if prior.startswith('s') and not prior.startswith('sh'):

            if current.startswith('sh'):

            if prior.endswith('ss') and not current.startswith('sh'):

                and not current.startswith('s')):

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3349 - a "repeated sibilant" detector.

What it is: this component reads almost only one MLP neuron of layer 1 (hidden unit 3349),
so its activation is a sign-flipped, scaled copy of that unit. The unit is mostly silent.
It goes strongly negative in two situations, both about a token that repeats the sound of
the token right before it:

  1. A word or name starting with the letter s (or Cyrillic с) that follows another word
     starting with s: "Social [Security]", "stainless [steel]", "SQL [Server]",
     "Secret [Service]", "South[side]". Strongest when the token continues the previous
     word without a leading space, or when both words are capitalised.
  2. A digit 8 right after another 8 ("88", "188").

Everything else is near zero. A lone s-word, or an s-word at the start of a document, is
only slightly negative.

Why this shape: the variance of the activation is dominated by rare large negative
spikes, and these two rules capture the largest, most consistent of them. A token table
would do better on the eval rows, but it has no concept behind it; these rules do.

Predictions are in activation units (negative = the component's contribution points the
other way). Variance explained on 8192 training rows is about 0.07.
"""

def starts_sibilant(text: str) -> bool:
    """True if the token's first visible character is an s-like letter."""
    return text.strip()[:1] in SIBILANT_LETTERS

    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else None

    if cur.strip() == "8":
        # Rule 2: an 8 repeating an 8.
        value = -0.5 if prev is not None and prev.strip() == "8" else -0.07
    elif starts_sibilant(cur):
        if prev is None:
            value = -0.25  # s-word opening a document
        elif starts_sibilant(prev):

            glued = cur[:1] != " "
            both_capitalised = cur.strip()[:1].isupper() and prev.strip()[:1].isupper()
            value = -0.8 if glued or both_capitalised else -0.2

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on the letters that follow an
"f" in spellings that are not ordinary English, the kind found in code and
abbreviations, and it is near zero everywhere else.

  * Whole tokens: fn (Rust/JS "fn", "Fn", "FN"), func (Go), fin, fins, fines, and
    the abbreviation-like fp, fm, fw, fx, fj (FP, FM, FW, FX, ...). Most are about -2 to -4.

    the next token (e.g. "table-f" + "n", "GF" + "N", "Huf" + "nagel"). "n" is the
    strongest (about -4), "m", "w", "j" about -2 to -2.5. "ff" + n (as in "öffnet")
    does not fire.
  * "paraff" + "in" and "Baff" + "in" (paraffin, Baffin): the "in" after "ff"/"af" is
    about -6.
  * The middle-dot filler token "··" (repeated dot leaders) gives a steady -2.2.

Everything else predicts 0. Values are rounded means measured on training rows.
"""

WHOLE = {"fn": -4.0, "fw": -4.0, "fp": -3.5, "fm": -3.5, "fx": -2.0, "fj": -2.0,
         "func": -2.5, "fin": -3.0, "fines": -3.0, "fins": -3.0}

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3351 is a "regex syntax" feature. Its activation is
close to zero on almost all text, but goes strongly negative on the tokens of a regular
expression or a pattern-matching call in code: the `.sub` / `.compile` / `.split` calls,
the `(/` that opens a JavaScript regex literal, `regexp`, the character-class fragments
of a pattern (`('[`, `^`, `-Z` in `[^a-zA-Z]`, `]+`, `.*`), and `grep` or `_replace`.

It only does this once the document has used regex vocabulary (`regex`, `Pattern`,
`grep`, `compile`, ...), so the same tokens in ordinary prose, or in a stack trace, stay
near zero. The program keeps one flag per document, which resets at a document boundary,
and predicts a fixed negative strength per token when the flag is set.

    "regex", "regexp", "Regex", "RegExp", "Pattern", "Matcher",
    "grep", "compile", "sed", "pattern",
}

    ".sub": 10, ".compile": 10, "(/": 10, "regexp": 10, "/^": 10, "(/\\": 10,
    "('[": 8, "-Z": 8,
    "regex": 6, "_replace": 6, "grep": 5, "Pattern": 5, "Matcher": 5, ".split": 5,
    "split": 4, "]+": 4, "]*": 4, ".*": 4, "^": 3,
    "match": 2, "replace": 2,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token: negative strength if the document is in regex mode."""
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    if document != last_document:

on the opening " //" or " #" of a comment. On "=" in maths or ordinary prose it is near zero or
negative ("cos t = cos s", "the answer is = 2"), and after a closing bracket ("f(x) = ...").

semicolons, comment markers, indentation) and falls with how much English it contains.

               "it", "be", "for", "in", "on", "with", "when", "if", "must", "equation", "term"}

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]

                  if prefix.document_ids[i] == doc]

               if prefix.document_ids[i] == doc]

each document (the position where attention has nothing before it but the token itself).

* punctuation, quotes, code symbols, digits            -> about 0

* a word with a leading space, CJK, other scripts      -> mildly negative (-0.2 to -0.4)

    "punct": 0.0,
    "digit": 0.0,

that comes right after a comma which follows an earlier `"key": value` pair (or a PHP

tokens so far: a small carry holds the open brackets, the last ~600 characters, and the
previous token, reset at each document boundary.

# (a plain quote, an apostrophe, or an escaped \" inside a JSON string).

    return (stack, window, new), value

    'region': 'region area district zone territory division suburb bank shore',
    'layout': 'row column line layer floor level base band page',
    'body': 'limb arm leg head lobe finger toe wing',

    #include <stdio.h>     -> the ' <' after #include is about -13 (about -11 after the first include)
    #include "foo.h"       -> the ' "' after #include is about -22 (about -17.5 after the first include)

Everything else is predicted as 0. The component's activation is near zero on almost every
token, so this is the part of its behaviour that is large and reliable. "#include" is
sometimes tokenised as "#" then "include", and that counts too.
"""

READS = ()

FIRST_QUOTE = -22.0   # opening " right after the first #include in a document
LATER_QUOTE = -17.5   # opening " right after a later #include
FIRST_ANGLE = -13.0   # opening < right after the first #include
LATER_ANGLE = -11.0   # opening < right after a later #include


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (how many #include directives this document has had so far,
    #         whether the previous token completed a directive)
    count, after_directive = carry or (0, False)
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    same_doc = len(docs) > 1 and docs[-1] == docs[-2]
    if not same_doc:
        count, after_directive = 0, False
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    value = 0.0
    if after_directive:
        first = count == 1
        opener = cur.lstrip()[:1]  # the bracket or quote that opens the file name
        if opener == '"':
            value = FIRST_QUOTE if first else LATER_QUOTE
        elif opener == "<":
            value = FIRST_ANGLE if first else LATER_ANGLE
    is_directive = cur == "#include" or (cur == "include" and prev == "#")
    if is_directive:
        count += 1
    return (count, is_directive), float(value)

QUANTITIES = set(
    'all any each eight every few five four many multiple nine no one only '
    'seven several six some ten three two '.split())

    'are be being is was were '.split())
BOUNDS = set(
    'arbitrary different distinct highest largest lowest maximal maximum '
    'minimal minimum same smallest unique '.split())
MODALS = set(
    'can cannot could may might must should would '.split())

    'creates cultural customer customers ethical face fair intrinsic market '
    'monetary moral par present probative property sentimental shared '
    'social spiritual stock worth '.split())
NUMERIC_MODIFIERS = set(
    'absolute arbitrary assumed certain chosen constant different distinct '
    'given integer large negative numeric numerical other parameter '
    'particular positive possible real small specific unique unknown '.split())
MATH_WORDS = set(
    'coordinate coordinates cos cosine denominator equation equations even '
    'expression fraction fractions function integer integers matrix '
    'negative numerator odd parameter parameters polynomial positive prime '
    'rational sin sine theorem variable variables '.split())
SUBJECT_NOUNS = set(
    'number numbers value values variable variables sum product fraction '
    'fractions root roots angle angles denominator numerator coordinate '
    'coordinates '.split())
MAGNITUDES = set(
    'small large big larger smaller higher lower greater less very too '.split())
VARIABLE_PREDICATES = set(
    'is are must can could would may might = such when where '.split())


def subject_level(text):
    text = text.strip()
    if re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z](?:_[a-z0-9]+)?', text) and text != 'I':
        return 1.0
    return 0.5 if text.lower() in SUBJECT_NOUNS else 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, [], [])
    _, history, marks = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    previous = history[-1].strip().lower() if history else ''
    rule = WORD_RULES.get(word)
    value = 0.0
    if rule is not None:
        # Average short and longer mathematical-context density.
        math = (min(1.0, sum(marks[-24:]) / 5)
                + min(1.0, sum(marks) / 12)) / 2
        subject = subject_level(history[-1]) if history else 0.0
        if previous in COPULAS | MODALS and len(history) > 1:
            subject = max(subject, subject_level(history[-2]))
        if previous == 'a' and word not in VARIABLE_PREDICATES:
            subject = 0.0
        after_value = previous in {'value', 'values'}
        c = SimpleNamespace(
            math=math, subject=subject,
            quantity=(previous in QUANTITIES
                      or (previous.isdigit() and len(previous) < 4)),
            copula=previous in COPULAS, article=previous in {'a', 'an', 'the'},
            bound=previous in BOUNDS, modal=previous in MODALS,
            s_ending=word.endswith('s'), spaced=token.startswith(' '),
            after_as=previous == 'as',
            negation=previous in {'not', 'no', 'never', 'impossible'},
            modifier=previous in NUMERIC_MODIFIERS,
            after_value=after_value,
            restricted_value=(after_value and len(history) > 1
                              and history[-2].strip().lower()
                              in NUMERIC_MODIFIERS | QUANTITIES | BOUNDS),
            economic=bool(set(''.join(history[-12:]).lower().split()) & ECONOMIC),
            magnitude=previous in MAGNITUDES,
        )
        value = float(rule(c))
    # Remember only recent evidence, never a model activation.
    mark = float(bool(re.search(r'[0-9=<>≤≥≠±²³∈∑√π]', token))
                 or word in MATH_WORDS
                 or (len(word) == 1 and word.isascii() and word.isalpha()
                     and word not in {'a', 'i'}))
    return (doc, (history + [token])[-96:], (marks + [mark])[-96:]), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:3364: a "math solution-space" feature.

What it does: this component reads the MLP hidden state of layer 1 and writes into the
residual stream. Its activation is almost always near zero, but it goes strongly negative
(down to about -7) on the vocabulary of mathematical case analysis and solution-set talk:
"values", "possible", "positive integers", "the value of", "must be", "such that", "the answer",
"equal", "cases", and on the "=" of a variable being set ("for k = 2", "let x = ...").
It does this only inside mathematical text. The same words in ordinary prose (e.g. "the
present value of accrued benefits") stay near zero.

The program predicts that: a negative level on those words, scaled by how mathematical the
last 400 tokens of the same document are. A token counts as mathematical if it has a digit,
a math symbol, or is one of the solution-space words. Context reaches full strength when at
least a fifth of those tokens are mathematical.

Simple version vs. table: the word lists and the context gate are the whole program. A
per-token lookup table would fit the activations better in-sample, but its gain on held-out
text is small (token identity alone explains about 9% of variance on held-out rows), because
the same word's activation depends on context.
"""
import re

# Solution-space and case-analysis words, by how strongly the component responds to them.
STRONG = {"integers", "integer", "positive", "values", "possible", "impossible", "solutions",
          "minimal"}
MEDIUM = {"value", "answer", "answers", "solution", "equal", "negative", "cases", "must", "odd",
          "different", "valid", "satisfy", "pairs", "distinct", "larger", "bigger", "smallest"}
WEAK = {"case", "such", "when", "be", "real", "exist", "even", "try"}
MATH_WORDS = STRONG | MEDIUM | WEAK | {"="}

WINDOW = 400         # tokens of context (within one document) that set how mathematical it is
FULL_DENSITY = 0.2   # share of mathematical tokens at which the context counts as fully mathematical

READS = ()


def is_mathy(token):
    """A digit, a math symbol, or a solution-space word."""
    return bool(re.search(r"[0-9=$\\^<>≤≥≠+*/]", token)) or token.strip().lower() in MATH_WORDS


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (flags of recent tokens, document id of the last token); reset at a document change
    flags, last_doc = carry if carry is not None else ([], None)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc != last_doc:
        flags = []
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    flags = (flags + [is_mathy(token)])[-WINDOW:]
    context = min(1.0, sum(flags) / len(flags) / FULL_DENSITY)

    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if word == "of" and previous.lower() in ("value", "values"):
        level = -4.0         # "the value of ..." in a math problem
    elif word == "=" and len(previous) == 1 and previous.isalpha():
        level = -1.5         # "for k = ...", "let x = ...": a variable being set
    elif word in STRONG:
        level = -2.0
    elif word in MEDIUM:
        level = -1.0
    elif word in WEAK:
        level = -0.5
    else:
        level = 0.0
    return (flags, doc), level * context

Large training responses often followed possessives or a/an. This program
approximates their signs using familiar groups of English noun bases.

    # sex terms
    ('male female',
     -2.14, -1.24),

GROUPS = tuple((frozenset(words.split()), possessive, article)
               for words, possessive, article in GROUPS)

BASE = (-0.005, 0.023)
MODIFIER_SCALE = (0.65, 0.67)


@lru_cache(maxsize=20000)
def scores(word):

    bases = set(wordnet.base_forms(word, "noun")) | {word}
    possessive, article = BASE
    for words, p, a in GROUPS:

    return (doc, word, previous), float(value)

"""A response to document openers, rather than to ordinary running text.

Opening capitals usually give a positive response, while space-prefixed words
and short fragments tend negative. Mathematical instructions and question
openers are exceptions. Escaped layout characters differ from actual tabs.
The opening response persists through an initial run of identical tokens.
Later tokens are zero except for the old-file range marker in a unified diff.
These coarse category averages leave substantial word-specific variation out.
"""
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
MATH_OPENERS = set('given let find compute calculate evaluate determine '
                   'express solve prove represent simplify expand'.split())
QUESTION_WORDS = set('what how when where which who why'.split())


def opening(text):
    word = text.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    space = text.startswith(' ')
    capital = word[:1].isupper()
    if lower in MATH_OPENERS:
        return -5.2 if capital and not space else -1.8
    if lower in QUESTION_WORDS:
        return -1.0 if capital and not space else -0.7
    if lower in {'question', 'answer'}:
        return -3.5 if capital and not space else -0.6
    if text == r'\t':
        return -4.7
    if text == r'\n':
        return -1.4
    if text in {r'\"', r"\'"}:
        return -5.8
    if capital:
        frequency = zipf_frequency(lower, 'en')
        if len(word) == 1:
            return -0.53 if frequency > 5 else 0.01
        if frequency >= 7:
            return -0.35
        return 0.12 if space else 0.92
    if space:
        return 0.0 if not word else (-0.47 if len(word) <= 4 else -0.76)
    if '\t' in text:
        return 3.0 if text.strip('\t') == '' else 1.6
    return -0.25 if len(word) <= 1 else 0.03


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        value = opening(prefix.token_strings[-1])
        return (document, token, value), value
    if carry[1] == token:
        return carry, carry[2]
    value = 0.0
    if (prefix.token_strings[-1] == ' -' and
            prefix.token_strings[-2].rstrip().endswith('@@')):
        value = 0.85  # The old-file range in a unified-diff header.
    return (document, None, 0.0), value

Separators get stronger scores after longer clauses, sentences, and unspaced
runs. Compound closing punctuation gets an extra boost. Some signal continues
onto linking words or auxiliaries following a comma or bracket. Numeric endings
and escaped whitespace have separate adjustments; document starts are negative.
The counters are capped, and this does not attempt full syntactic analysis.
"""

LINKING_WORDS = {'and', 'or', 'but', 'nor', 'yet', 'so', 'then', 'until'}

break, a closing bracket, a sentence end, a quote, a comma, a connective word), and
how strongly depends on how number-dense the text just before it is.

  d is high and the response is strong; in ordinary prose d is ~0 and the response
  is weak.

    closing bracket ) ] }          0.05 + 0.65 d

    quote " ' ” 」                  0.45 d
    comma , ，                      0.25 d
    connective (and, but, while,
      which, however, ...)          0.80 d

- The first token of every document pushes it to -0.5.

The program carries (document id, tokens so far in the document) in its carry, so it
runs in linear time over a row.
"""

READS = ()

CONNECTIVES = {
    "and", "but", "while", "whereas", "which", "however", "therefore",
    "respectively", "or", "so", "thus", "where", "although",
}

    return any(ch.isdigit() for ch in text)

    """The response to one token given digit share d, or None if it is not a boundary."""
    if "\n" in token:
        return 0.10 + 0.90 * d
    if any(ch in ")]}" for ch in token):
        return 0.05 + 0.65 * d
    if any(ch in ".。;!?" for ch in token):
        return 0.10 + 0.20 * d
    if any(ch in "\"'”」" for ch in token):
        return 0.45 * d
    if any(ch in ",，" for ch in token):
        return 0.25 * d
    if token.strip() in CONNECTIVES:
        return 0.80 * d
    return None

"""Approximate an early MLP response to relational-adjective endings.

Recognize -al, its inflections and its Romance/Germanic/Slavic relatives.
Use the spelling assembled so far, so a suffix split over tokens still counts.
Short suffix fragments generally get a stronger response than whole words.
The strengths and length/form modifiers are fitted on training text;
there is no vocabulary lookup and no semantic adjective classifier.
A mild 1.25 gain favors the larger responses that matter to model output.
"""
import re
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache

READS = ()

# Ordinary inflection/adverb endings, then further word derivations.
_FORM = r'(?:a|e|i|es|s|ly|en|er|mente|ity'
_SIMPLE = _FORM + r')?$'
_DERIVED = _FORM + r'|ism|ist|ize)?$'
_FULL = _FORM + r'|ism|ist|ize|isation|ization)?$'



def word_tail(previous, token):
    if not token:
        return ''
    # A punctuation mark or space terminates the word being assembled.
    match = re.search(r'[^\W\d_]+$', token, re.UNICODE)
    if not match:
        return ''
    piece = match.group()
    if match.start() == 0:
        piece = previous + piece
    return piece[-64:]


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def family(word):
    # Latin accents do not change the underlying suffix family.
    w = ''.join(c for c in unicodedata.normalize('NFD', word.lower())
                if not unicodedata.combining(c))
    w = unicodedata.normalize('NFC', w)
    if re.search(r'аль(?:н[а-я]*)?$', w):
        return 'palatal'
    if re.search(r'aln[aeiouy]*$', w):
        return 'palatal'
    if re.search(r'ал[аоиы]?$', w):
        return 'slavic'
    if re.search(r'(?:シャル|ナル|タル|셜|널|컬)$', w):
        return 'loan'
    # Inflections: Italian -ale/-ali, Spanish -ales, Portuguese -ais,
    # French -aux/-elle/-iel, German -ell/-ellen.
    if re.search('ial' + _FULL, w):
        return 'ential' if re.search(r'ential|encial', w) else 'ial'
    for suffix in ('ional', 'ical', 'ual', 'inal', 'ental', 'al'):
        forms = _FULL if suffix == 'al' else (
            _DERIVED if suffix == 'ional' else _SIMPLE)
        if re.search(suffix + forms, w):
            return suffix
    if re.search(r'(?:iel|uel|eel|iell|uell|onnel)(?:e|es|s|en|er|ement|le|les)?$', w):
        return 'iel'
    if re.search(r'(?:ell|nel)(?:e|es|s|en|er|ement|le|les)?$', w):
        return 'ell'
    if re.search(r'(?:iais|eais|ais|iaux|eaux|aux)$', w):
        return 'plural'
    return ''


def descriptor(previous, token):
    word = word_tail(previous, token)
    f = family(word)
    if not f:
        return word, None
    length = 0 if len(word) <= 4 else (1 if len(word) <= 7 else 2)
    bare = token.strip().lower()
    if len(word) > len(bare) and token[:1].isalpha():
        if family(bare):
            mode = 1 if len(bare) <= 4 else 2
        else:
            mode = 3
    else:
        mode = 0
    if re.search(r'(?:ality|alism|alist|alize|alization)$', word.lower()):
        shape = 'derivative'
    elif re.search(r'(?:ally|almente|ellement)$', word.lower()):
        shape = 'adverb'
    elif re.search(r'(?:ala|ale|ali|ales|ais|aux|elle|elles|ellen|ials|icals|als)$', word.lower()):
        shape = 'inflected'
    else:
        shape = 'plain'
    return word, (f, mode, length, shape)


# Columns: whole token, short suffix, longer suffix, continuation.
STRENGTH = {
    'al': (0.52, 0.79, 0.43, 0.35),
    'ial': (0.99, 1.89, 1.23, 0.89),
    'ential': (1.16, 1.94, 2.53, 1.41),
    'ional': (0.47, 1.31, 1.23, 0.98),
    'ical': (0.6, 0.8, 0.43, 0.59),
    'ual': (0.71, 1.35, 0.72, 0.76),
    'inal': (0.84, 2.38, 1.15, 0.37),
    'ental': (0.77, 1.74, 1.01, 0.5),
    'iel': (0.1, 1.96, 1.22, 0.67),
    'ell': (0.02, 0.17, 0.14, 0.25),
    'palatal': (0.29, 1.94, 2.02, 0.9),
    'slavic': (0.25, 0.81, 0.44, 0.91),
    'loan': (0.69, 1.12, 0.49, 0.5),
    'plural': (0.12, 0.81, 0.7, 1.14),
}

# Attenuate endings of short words; columns are <=4, <=7, >7 letters.
LENGTH = (
    (0.39, 0.63, 1.0),
    (0.31, 0.47, 1.0),
    (1, 0.81, 1.0),
    (0.27, 0.61, 1.0),
)

# Form modifiers: uninflected, inflected, adverb, further derivation.
FORM = (
    (1.0, 0.65, 0.5, 0.33),
    (1.0, 1.97, 0.84, 1),
    (1.0, 1.17, 1.04, 0.76),
    (1.0, 2.81, 1.21, 0.46),
)

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    word, features = descriptor(previous, prefix.token_strings[-1])
    value = -0.001
    if features is not None:
        suffix, mode, length, shape = features
        form = ('plain', 'inflected', 'adverb', 'derivative').index(shape)
        value = (-1.25 * STRENGTH[suffix][mode]
                 * LENGTH[mode][length] * FORM[mode][form])
    return (doc, word), float(value)
